international.title: Constitutional law expert brands defence bill allowing secret security rules ‘lazy and irresponsible’
international.summary: Anne Twomey says lack of proper debate around bill is ‘flabbergasting’ amid concerns over extension of ministerial powers Labor’s new defence bill is “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking, one of Australia’s leading constitutional scholars has warned, claiming provisions for the government to secretly class any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues. Prime minister Anthony Albanese claimed on Monday that critics of the ‘accelerating capability and protecting bases’ bill were “jump[ing] at shadows”, accusing them of “absurd” claims. But parliamentary crossbenchers opposed to the bill, which was rushed through parliament with little public scrutiny, were joined on Monday by Prof Anne Twomey, who expressed alarm about what she called an increasing trend of ministers exercising discretionary powers without parliamentary oversight.
